verdict.line: You lose trades where you eat Sion's Q (Cryptic Gaze) stun into a full Enrage burst without a Rupture escape ready, and you win every extended trade where Vorpal Spikes outlasts the health he's spending on Enrage autos.

brief.thesis: Sion's E (Enrage) buys him attack damage by spending his own health on every auto, while your E (Vorpal Spikes) procs on every attack for free — the longer a trade runs, the worse it gets for him. That asymmetry is why Cho'Gath carries a measured solo-kill edge in an otherwise even lane (52.1% win rate over 167 games): he wins attrition, Sion wins the short burst window right after he lands Q (Cryptic Gaze). Whoever decides when the trade starts and stops wins it.

theirWindow.when: right after he lands Q stun
theirWindow.what: He'll chain Enrage-empowered autos into you for the full stun duration. Don't contest this window — back off or Flash out, since there's no escaping the stun itself.

yourWindow.when: whenever his Q is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Step in and trade freely. Lead with an auto for the Vorpal Spikes proc, and if he still commits to an Enrage trade, Rupture (Q) him to cut the engage short and Feral Scream (W) to silence any follow-up.

start.why: Mana and sustain to spam Rupture and Vorpal Spikes autos through early trades; 76.8% pick rate and the highest-winrate start by far (52.5% over 162 games).

boots.why: Sion's entire early damage profile is auto-attacks powered by Enrage — flat damage reduction per hit directly undercuts the trade he's trying to force.

core.why: Gives you a gap-closer to land Feast on a kiting Sion and burst damage that scales your trades before he out-tanks you.
Sustained-damage amp turns your Vorpal Spikes poke into real DPS over the course of an extended trade.
Closes the gap on a disengaging Sion and adds the HP you need now that he's building into a dueling threat; this path hits 71.4% win rate over its sample.
Omnivamp and HP keep you winning the extended fights your kit is built for, matching the common late-game item pool on this champion.

runes.keystoneWhy: Grasp's proc damage and heal reward exactly the long auto-trade pattern Vorpal Spikes already wants, and it's the higher-winrate page (51.6% vs 51% over similar samples). Master-tier players instead run Hail of Blades (Domination) across 1,917 games — that suits a more aggressive, all-in Cho'Gath who wants to front-load burst rather than win the grind.

summoners.why: Teleport is the overwhelming pick (74.7%) and lets you reset waves after trading or help other lanes once Feast starts stacking your HP. Flash+Ignite (54.5% win rate, 20.3% pick) is the stronger choice if you want to lean harder into the solo-kill edge and close out Feast executions earlier.

playing.title: Trade when his Q is down
playing.detail: Track Sion's Q (Cryptic Gaze, 12/11/10/9/8s cooldown by rank). Once he's used it or whiffed it, step in and auto freely — he has no stun left to punish the engage.

playing.title: Punish Enrage with Vorpal Spikes
playing.detail: E (Enrage) has no cooldown but costs Sion health per attack. Your E (Vorpal Spikes) procs on every auto for free, so holding the trade a few seconds longer than he wants bleeds him faster than you.

playing.title: Rupture-Scream his Q commit
playing.detail: The moment Sion commits to casting Cryptic Gaze, Rupture (Q) then Feral Scream (W) — the knockup and silence cancel his follow-up and let you walk away clean.

playing.title: Respect brush near his Q range
playing.detail: Cryptic Gaze reaches 550 range and he can cast it from brush before you see him. Don't facecheck brush along his lane presence without vision.

playing.title: Save Feast for overextensions
playing.detail: Feast (R) deals high true damage and executes on a kill, so hold it for the moment he overcommits an Enrage trade rather than opening with it.

playing.title: Respect his shield window
playing.detail: Death's Caress (W, 8s cooldown) absorbs damage then explodes on surrounding enemies. Wait for the shield to pop or bait its early detonation before committing your trade.

playing.title: Prioritize kills over even trades
playing.detail: Every kill with Feast grows your max HP (up to 6 stacks), and dying only costs half your stacks — picking off Sion compounds your stat lead far more than trading even does.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, rune, and summoner data above are measured from live games on the current patch (OP.GG); the mechanical reasoning — trade timing, cooldown windows, and ability interactions — is my own read of the matchup.

stats.opponentTip: Try to use [Q][W] when he is charging up his (Q). Keep in mind that he may be trying to use (Q) from inside a brush.
